reasons: Directionally correct: flipping the p0082 default from Type II (IBM-owned) to Type I (Customer-owned) reverses the ownership default in our favour with a one-word edit, and Type I in this agreement vests title in Customer, so the edit reaches the playbook's preferred position.

The p0085 amendment keeps IBM's ownership of pre-existing/third-party Materials (permitted by the rule) while upgrading the licence-back to perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free with the right to prepare derivative works and use for Customer's business — squarely the preferred/fallback licence position; the higher changed-character ratio is justified because the licence grant itself had to be rewritten.

New paragraph (e) supplies the missing Customer Data/IP ownership statement for Content and Customer Components and expressly negates assignment and joint ownership, matching the redline guidance and closing the gap left by the 'no rights beyond those expressly stated' clause.
No residual assignment of Customer IP or data to IBM, and no joint ownership is created; deterministic checks all pass.
Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise, states what changed and why, and offers the perpetual/irrevocable/modify-and-sublicense licence as the fallback if IBM will not move the default.
